title: Accidental Wilderness: Europe's Everglades
description: Documentary about a former wasteland in the middle of Europe where wastewater used to be deposited, which is now a paradise for birds migrating from across the continent and beyond.

title: The Island of Giants
description: Exploring how whale sharks drive the culture of Santa Maria, the only European hotspot for these giants and why warming seas may be drawing them in.

title: Great Lakes Wild
description: The amazing world of the flying squirrel, typically found along the shores of Lake Erie, but now moving their territory towards Lake Ontario.

title: Great Lakes Wild
description: How the elk got a second chance. It went extinct in Ontario, but is now recovering after being re-introduced.

title: Planet Weird
description: A look at some of the Earth's harshest environments, where creatures battle the elements to survive.

title: Osprey
description: When a veteran pair of osprey return home, they must take on enemies, elements and hundreds of fish if they wish to raise the next generation.

title: Ireland's Wild Islands with Eoin Warner
description: The wildlife presenter sails a 140-year-old Galway hooker out into the Atlantic to showcase Ireland's western islands. Eoin starts his island voyage on Rathlin, then heads west for Malin Head and Inishtrahull, seeing basking sharks and dolphins, before going south to Achill Island.

title: Ireland's Wild Islands with Eoin Warner
description: Eoin visits a native woodland on Clare Island and as he sails through Connemara's waters, he finds deserted islands home to skylarks and Ireland's only native reptile on the Aran Islands.

title: Ireland's Wild Islands with Eoin Warner
description: Eoin is back in his Galway hooker and sails to the islands off Co Kerry, before heading south to his home waters off Cork and ending his journey at Fastnet Rock.

title: Flying Monsters with David Attenborough
description: The broadcaster explores the world of the pterosaur, a flying creature that occupied the skies 200 million years ago. Visiting sites around the world, from the Dorset coast to New Mexico, he explains how the reptiles evolved to defy the forces of gravity, and examines the features of their anatomy that can still be seen in present-day descendents. He also discovers why they became extinct after dominating the skies for millions of years.

title: David Attenborough's Natural History Museum Alive
description: The broadcaster invites viewers to join him as he takes an after-hours stroll around one of his favourite places, the Natural History Museum. But this is no ordinary tour as some of the many exhibits spring to life as the veteran naturalist strolls along.

title: Africa's Claws and Jaws
description: Documentary revealing the weapons at the disposal of Africa's predators, who never know where the next meal will come from, but must be prepared to find it.

title: Shark Squad
description: A look at how sharks are more complex and intelligent than generally believed, and not simply mindless eating machines prone to attacking humans.

title: World's Most Toxic Animals
description: First of two programmes about some of earth's most dangerous creatures, which lurk in the oceans, the forests, swamps and deserts. In Australia, meet the world's most venomous snake, and in nearby oceans, discover the deadly nature of the marine creatures that share these tropical waters.

title: World's Most Toxic Animals
description: Exploring more of earth's dangerous creatures, beginning in the South American rainforest with the poison-packed golden dart frog, which harbours enough poison to kill 10 men. Plus, a visit to Sydney, Australia, home of the world's most venomous spider.

title: Rewilding
description: Documentary about the European bison, the continent's biggest terrestrial mammal, which was hunted to extinction but has been re-introduced thanks to rewilding.

title: My Best Friend's an Animal
description: A visit to the ranch that Albert the camel runs with his human friend Alex, and a check-in with Herbie the wallaby as he gets pampered.

title: My Best Friend's an Animal
description: Following Shanet, who spends her days tending to the needs of penguin Harold Custard, and Barista, who cares for Cindy the baboon.

title: Baby Animals
description: Even giant animals start out small, and the likes of elephants, gorillas, rhinos and bison have some of the cutest babies in the animal kingdom.

title: Baby Animals
description: Most animals are born defenceless, but under the protection and guidance of their mothers, they soon become masters of their own universes.

title: City Wildlife Rescue
description: The vets wrestle an uncooperative turkey vulture onto the X-ray table to reveal a shoulder injury. A baby groundhog is rushed in after a car accident.

title: City Wildlife Rescue
description: A mother rabbit cares for an adopted baby, as the staff assesses the little bunny's safety. Can this odd couple stay together?

title: The Wild Wild East
description: The wildlife of the Maritime Provinces on Canada's eastern shore. The first edition visits Prince Edward Island to explore the family life of the red fox, sly creatures adept at living just on the fringes of society.

title: High Life in the Dead Mountains
description: A look at the stark karst plateau of caves and dry peaks in Austria's Totes Gebirge, hiding rich ecosystem where wildlife thrives against the odds.

title: New Kids in the Wild
description: In Brazil's Atlantic Forest, southern Muriqui Dora takes her first steps away from her mum Mimi.

In Australia, meet the world's most venomous snake, and in nearby oceans, discover the deadly nature of the marine creatures that share these tropical waters.

title: Loons: A Cry from the Mist
description: A year in the life of Canada's common loon, examining the perils impacting its population - from global warming and boat traffic to big wakes disturbing its habitat.

title: David Attenborough Meets Obama
description: Another chance to see Barack Obama's conversation, recorded in May 2015, with renowned naturalist and film-maker David Attenborough. In a twist on usual convention, the then-US president took the role of interviewer, quizzing Attenborough about his thoughts on the future of the planet, their shared passion for nature, and potential ways to protect the environment. title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals: Triumph of the Vertebrates
description: Part one of two. The naturalist explores the evolution of vertebrates over the past 500 million years, beginning with a look at how remarkable advances allowed primitive fish to make the radical move on to land, and then take to the skies with the advent of flight. He uses fossils of both ancient and living species combined with CGI and film to chart their journey out of the water to populate all corners of the globe.

title: David Attenborough's Rise of Animals: Triumph of the Vertebrates
description: The naturalist concludes his two-part exploration of the evolution of vertebrates over the past 500 million years by looking at the history of mammals. He traces their journey from humble origins as tiny nocturnal forest-dwellers to their astonishing explosion in diversity and domination of the world following the death of the dinosaurs.

title: Planet Weird
description: Nature's strangest survivors, from air-breathing lungfish and cannibal snails to transparent glass frogs and ingenious spiders that build their own underwater air chambers.

title: Whale with Steve Backshall
description: Steve freedives with whales and dolphins, getting closer than ever before to record rarely seen behaviours from these extraordinary mammals. He also teams up with world-leading scientists to confront the uncomfortable and urgent truths of overfishing and pollution, along the way uncovering how whales and dolphins are adapting to changing oceans in unexpected ways.

title: Whale with Steve Backshall
description: Steve reveals the ingenious hunting strategies of whales and dolphins, using sound, skill, teamwork and strategy to catch their prey.

title: Jungle of the Ants
description: Ants have an incredible form of collective intelligence, which has always fascinated people. This documentary offers an immersive micro-dive into the mysteries of an ant colony in the heart of the French Guianese jungle.

title: Qatar: Pearls in the Sand
description: The desert peninsula of Qatar, exploring its landscape and inhabitants, as well as its transformation from being a centre for pearls, to being known for oil and gas production.

title: Planet Weird
description: Nature's strangest survivors, from air-breathing lungfish and cannibal snails to transparent glass frogs and ingenious spiders that build their own underwater air chambers.

title: The Ocean's Greatest Feast
description: The sardine run along the east coast of South Africa, a challenging voyage for the fish as they navigate the ocean, barely escaping the hungry predators who depend on them for food.

title: Bugs That Ruled the World
description: A global investigation into insect declines, exploring their diversity and their critical roles on the planet. Scientists reveal the beauty of bugs, from pollinators to insect assassins to the tiny clean-up crews that purify the planet.

title: Bugs That Ruled the World
description: Learning how bees, butterflies, moths and other pollinators keep the fields fruitful and exploring what life would be like if these busy bugs vanished.
